title: Building a Modern GitHub Pages Site with Vite
summary: How to build and deploy a modern static web application to GitHub Pages using Vite, native ES Modules, and GitHub Actions.
html:
Building a Modern GitHub Pages Site with Vite

GitHub Pages is one of the easiest ways to host static websites. By pairing it with Vite and GitHub Actions, you get an automated, lightning-fast deployment pipeline.

Why Vite?

Traditional build setups like Grunt or webpack require extensive configuration. Vite offers:

  1. Instant Server Start: Uses native ES modules during development.
  2. Lightning Fast HMR: Hot Module Replacement that updates instantly regardless of app size.
  3. Optimized Production Builds: Rollup-powered static bundling out of the box.

Automating Deployment with GitHub Actions

With GitHub Actions actions/deploy-pages@v4, you can build and publish directly to GitHub Pages on every push to main:

name: Deploy to GitHub Pages

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: ./dist

Tip: Ensure your repository's Pages settings are configured to use GitHub Actions as the deployment source!
